nodes.label: Wall-Mounted Ventilation Exhaust Fan (KDK)
nodes.description: In-situ photograph of a white square louvred wall/window exhaust fan (red KDK badge) mounted on a dark panel set into a tiled opening, with a white mains cable running up from the top of the unit. The louvre blades show visible dust and grime staining, indicating an in-service, non-laboratory installation.
nodes.rationale: An off-the-shelf mains exhaust fan is used as the ventilation actuator: it moves enough air to actually change enclosure gas concentration and temperature, and being a mains appliance it is switched through the relay rather than driven directly.

nodes.label: Ventilation Actuation (Air Exchange Control)
nodes.description: The control action of expelling stale air from the enclosure to reduce accumulated gas concentration and shed heat. It is the corrective response paired with a gas-concentration or temperature measurement.
nodes.rationale: Ventilation is the natural counter-actuator to gas build-up: it directly reduces the quantity the MQ-135 measures, closing a sense-decide-act loop on air quality.
